metadata.title: Middle School A+++ Introductory Agricultural Home Gardening — 13-Week Course
research_basis: USDA National Agricultural Library: Vegetable Gardening and home-garden planning resources
USDA Farm to School: School Gardens and garden-based education
USDA Team Nutrition: Dig In! standards-based garden and nutrition education
National Agricultural Literacy Outcomes: middle-school and high-school agricultural literacy benchmarks
NC State Extension Grow For It: youth gardening curriculum resources
National Core Arts/Science-style inquiry approach adapted to agricultural investigations

course_goals: Understand gardening as a living system connecting plants, soil, water, weather, insects, people, and food.
Build foundational skills in observation, garden planning, seed starting, soil care, watering, crop selection, harvesting, and stewardship.
Use garden journals and simple data to make evidence-based decisions.
Develop respect for food systems, biodiversity, natural resources, and safe garden practices.
Create a realistic small-scale home or school garden plan.

weeks.weekly_goal: Master garden ecology & the gardener's journal through observation, inquiry, planning, hands-on practice, and reflection.

lessons.title: What Is Agriculture and Horticulture?
objectives: Develop middle school understanding of what is agriculture and horticulture?.
Use observation, measurement, records, and evidence to make gardening decisions.
Connect plant production with soil, water, ecology, nutrition, stewardship, and community.
activities: Observe and record a garden phenomenon.
Learn the relevant science/agriculture concept.
Conduct a safe, age-appropriate garden investigation or planning exercise.
Analyze results and make a supported decision.
Update the garden journal and identify the next action.
lessons.assessment: Garden journal, observation record, diagram, calculation, plan, or short explanation.
lessons.safety_note: Use age-appropriate tools and materials with adult supervision; follow local food-safety guidance and product labels. Do not handle pesticides, powered equipment, or other hazardous materials independently.
